clue.text: Decline to swallow revolution

parts.note: to swallow a drink is to down it
a revolution is one turn of a wheel

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to gulp down the idea of an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline in trade or fortunes is a downward slide, the same as a slump.

clue.text: Strip in bar over the way

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar
St, street, is a way, as in a road name

explanation.surface: A stripper performs in a bar across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to take off or deprive, as of clothes or property.

clue.text: Star we may come to see as good for nothing

indicators.note: the letters may come to form something new, a change in arrangement

explanation.surface: A celebrity we once admired is now seen as useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may come to' signals that STARWE is rearranged; 'see as' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A waster is an idle, worthless person, a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Drink college tea

parts.note: Clare is a Cambridge college
T sounds like tea and stands for it in crosswords, as in T-break or a cuppa

explanation.surface: A simple invitation to a cup of tea in a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare is one of the colleges of Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: The most stupid at any rate

explanation.definitionFit: Least wise describes the dimmest person, and leastwise is an old adverb meaning anyway or at least.

clue.text: Hold back soldiers' practise

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers, and the possessive adds S
to train is to practise

explanation.surface: Soldiers keep their exercises in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps, RE for short.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to curb or check.

clue.text: Point to those employed by enforcement officer

parts.note: a tip is a point, as of a pen
staff are the people employed

explanation.surface: An officer of the law gives advice to workers.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court officer who enforces orders, named for his metal-tipped staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's or court officer charged with arrests and keeping order.

clue.text: Uncommon chap playing against one southern number

parts.note: V, short for versus, means playing against in a fixture
I is the Roman numeral one
a count is a number or total

explanation.surface: An unusual man takes on a lone southerner in a numbers game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommon' means not a commoner: a peer of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a nobleman, a rank of the peerage, so he is no commoner.

clue.text: Renounce parent's mouthful

parts.note: PA is a parent, a father, and the possessive adds S
a sup is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: A child refuses a sip from Dad's glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or decline an opportunity is to forgo it.

clue.text: Live down and up with the BBC

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the second copy reads backwards, bottom to top

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Broadcasting live, all over the place, on the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down and up' gives BE down then BE turned up to EB. The Beeb is the British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeb is the familiar British nickname for the national broadcaster.

clue.text: Day before daughter went into shop with docker.

indicators.note: went into says the following pieces are put inside the word for shop

parts.note: a store is a shop
eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: A girl goes shopping with a dockworker on the eve of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day before' is a festival's eve, Christmas Eve for one; 'went into' is the container signal, and 'with' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, a port labourer.

clue.text: Sailor to return prophetic card

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: return tells us the little word to is turned round to read backwards

explanation.surface: A seaman returns to have his fortune told by cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are used in fortune-telling, so each one foretells the future.

clue.text: Note man in leather

parts.note: C is a musical note
Alf is a man's name, short for Alfred

explanation.surface: A man notes something written in leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf is the hide of a young cow, made into soft leather.

clue.text: Somewhere to live in solitary state

parts.note: apart means alone or separate
-ment is a suffix forming nouns of state, as in contentment

explanation.surface: A home for someone living in isolation.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms to live in.

clue.text: Conditional release, given to one very loud steward

parts.note: bail is release from custody on conditions
I is the Roman numeral one
FF, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A prisoner freed on bail meets a noisy estate manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is an agent or manager who runs an estate for its owner.

clue.text: Harsh words wasted on Lords' stonewaller

definitions.text: Harsh words wasted on Lords' stonewaller

parts.words: Harsh words wasted on Lords' stonewaller
parts.note: criticism thrown at a batsman blocking like a brick wall at Lord's, the cricket ground, slides off him

explanation.surface: Spectators' jeers do nothing to a defensive batsman at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a stonewaller is a batsman who only blocks. Read as BRICK + BAT he is a brick-wall batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a cutting remark, literally a piece of brick thrown at someone.

clue.text: Honour Sir has to shoulder

parts.note: a knight is dubbed by a sword touching the shoulder, the ceremony that makes him Sir

explanation.surface: A knight must bear the burden of his honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulder' looks like a verb meaning bear; it is where the sword touches at the dubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or praise, originally the tap on the shoulder that confers knighthood.

clue.text: Modern music entirely associated with sea area

parts.note: rock is a genre of modern popular music
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Contemporary music is entirely linked with the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: ROCKALL is one of the sea areas of the BBC Shipping Forecast, the radio weather report for British waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is a named zone of the North Atlantic in British marine weather forecasts.

clue.text: Part of the whole statement in case

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fragment of a full declaration made just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: Lest is a conjunction meaning for fear that, so as to avoid.

clue.text: Offspring that should be well drilled

explanation.surface: Children who ought to be strictly disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well drilled' suggests discipline, but farmers sow seed in drills, rows cut in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed means descendants, as in Abraham's seed, and it is also what a seed drill plants in rows.

clue.text: Pinch part of harness

explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is to steal, and a snaffle is a simple jointed bit on a horse's bridle.

clue.text: Person objecting to baby-sitter

explanation.definitionFit: One who minds is someone with an objection, and one who minds a child looks after it.

clue.text: Lovingly united piano displayed

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
aired means shown or displayed publicly

explanation.surface: A piano is put on show by a devoted couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired means coupled, matched as partners.

clue.text: Influence strike

explanation.definitionFit: Clout is power to sway others, and also a heavy blow with the hand.

clue.text: Girl has an arrangement to reach earthly paradise

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means they are reordered

explanation.surface: A young woman plans a trip to a heaven on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the idyllic hidden valley of Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, now any blissful retreat.

clue.text: Land of the living

parts.note: the living here is a clergyman's benefice, which may include land that supports him

explanation.surface: The everyday world of people still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the living' sounds like the alive, but a living is a church post with its income.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is farmland belonging to a parish benefice, earning income for the vicar.

clue.text: Victor raising game of other sportsmen

explanation.surface: A winner lifts the play of the rest of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising game' looks like improving performance; beaters on a shoot flush game birds up for the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: One who beats an opponent wins, and on a shoot the person driving birds toward the guns has the same title.

clue.text: Close bid about criminal

indicators.note: about means the word for bid goes around the other piece

parts.note: a bid is an offer
a close is an end, as in the close of day

explanation.surface: A last offer is made concerning a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like an adjective meaning near, but here it is the noun meaning finish; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who breaks the law, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Agreement to buy a drink for youth leader

parts.note: to treat someone is to pay for their drink

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A deal is sealed by standing a young leader a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between states.

clue.text: Related how official at match made a mistake

parts.note: the referee, ref for short, officiates at a match
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A tale of how the referee got a decision wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Referred can mean related or attributed, as in symptoms referred to a cause.
